quests.instruction: Pick the animal that runs on the tip of a single toe on each foot, protected by a hard hoof.
quests.hint: Its foot ends in one big, round nail.
quests.explanation: A horse's hoof is a hard covering over its single toe. Long legs and a single toe make it a fast runner.
quests.funFact: Horses move in four gaits: walk, trot, canter and gallop.
quests.question: Horse

quests.instruction: Name the animal that walks flat-footed, with the whole sole touching the ground, much like you do.
quests.hint: Look at where the heel goes when it steps.
quests.explanation: Bears walk on the soles of their feet, which helps them balance when they stand up on their back legs.
quests.funFact: Over a short distance, a bear can run about as fast as a racehorse.
quests.question: Bear

quests.instruction: Name the animal that walks by moving both legs on the same side together, giving it a swaying stride.
quests.hint: Its left legs move together, then its right legs.
quests.explanation: Giraffes and camels move both legs on one side at the same time, which gives them their swaying walk.
quests.funFact: To drink, a giraffe has to spread its front legs wide or bend them to lower its head.
quests.question: Giraffe

quests.instruction: Which swimmer paddles with big webbed back feet and steers with a flat, paddle-like tail?
quests.hint: Its tail is broad, flat and covered in scales.
quests.explanation: Beavers kick with large webbed hind feet, and they use the flat tail as a rudder when they dive and turn.
quests.funFact: A beaver can stay underwater for about fifteen minutes.
quests.question: Beaver

quests.instruction: Which sea animal shoots itself backward by squeezing water out of a tube in its body?
quests.hint: It moves like a living jet engine.
quests.explanation: A squid squeezes water out through a funnel-like tube. The jet pushes it along, and it steers by pointing the tube.
quests.funFact: Some squid can shoot out of the water and glide through the air for a short distance.
quests.question: Squid

quests.instruction: Which reptile swims by sweeping its strong tail from side to side, with its legs tucked against its body?
quests.hint: Its tail does all of the work.
quests.explanation: A crocodile's tail is long and muscular, and sweeping it from side to side pushes the crocodile through the water.
quests.funFact: For short bursts, a crocodile can swim faster than a person can.
quests.question: Crocodile

quests.instruction: Which insect's wings beat about two hundred times each second, making a buzzing sound?
quests.hint: The buzz you hear is made by its wings moving so fast.
quests.explanation: A bee's wings beat roughly 200 times per second. That blur of motion is what makes the buzzing sound.
quests.funFact: A bee's front and back wings hook together when it flies, making one larger wing.
quests.question: Bee

quests.instruction: Which forest animal glides from tree to tree on a flap of skin stretched between its legs?
quests.hint: It doesn't really fly. It glides and steers with its tail.
quests.explanation: A flying squirrel spreads a furry skin flap between its front and back legs. It glides and uses its tail to steer.
quests.funFact: A flying squirrel can glide more than 50 metres between trees.
quests.question: Squirrel

quests.instruction: Pick the very large bird that has to run along the water, flapping hard, to pick up enough speed to take off.
quests.hint: It is so heavy that taking off takes a long run.
quests.explanation: Swans are heavy, so they need a long run across the water before they can lift into the air.
quests.funFact: A flying mute swan can reach about 50 kilometres an hour.
quests.question: Swan

quests.instruction: Pick the tiny hopper whose big back legs fold up like springs.
quests.hint: Its back legs are far bigger than its other four.
quests.explanation: Crickets have large back legs with powerful muscles. They fold up like springs and launch the cricket into the air.
quests.funFact: A cricket chirps faster on a warm night than on a cool one.
quests.question: Cricket

quests.instruction: Which amphibian can leap many times its own body length thanks to long, strong back legs?
quests.hint: Its hind legs unfold like a pair of catapults.
quests.explanation: A frog's long hind legs have powerful muscles. When they straighten, they launch the frog forward.
quests.funFact: Some tree frogs have sticky toe pads that help them land safely on leaves.
quests.question: Frog

quests.instruction: Find the forest animal that bounds with springy legs and can clear a fence taller than a person.
quests.hint: It is built for bounding, not for trotting.
quests.explanation: Deer have long, strong, springy legs. They can bound through woods and leap over obstacles.
quests.funFact: A white-tailed deer can jump a fence about two metres high.
quests.question: Deer

quests.instruction: Find the animal that can turn its back feet around backward, so it can scamper down a tree trunk head-first.
quests.hint: Its back ankles are unusually bendy.
quests.explanation: Squirrels can rotate their back feet, so their claws dig into the bark when they climb down head-first.
quests.funFact: A tree squirrel has eyes on the sides of its head, which gives it a wide view of danger.
quests.question: Squirrel

quests.instruction: Spot the animal that can walk up a smooth window pane because its toes are covered in millions of tiny hairs.
quests.hint: Its toes stick without glue.
quests.explanation: A gecko's toes have microscopic hairs. Tiny attractions between those hairs and a surface hold the gecko on.
quests.funFact: A gecko can hang from a ceiling by a single toe.
quests.question: Gecko

quests.instruction: Spot the animal that swings hand over hand through the treetops with arms longer than its legs.
quests.hint: Its arm span is much wider than its height.
quests.explanation: Orangutans have long arms and flexible shoulders, so they can move through the canopy hand over hand.
quests.funFact: Orangutans are the largest animals that live mostly in trees.
quests.question: Orangutan

quests.instruction: Name the animal that moves by stretching and squeezing its body, using tiny bristles to grip the soil.
quests.hint: It stretches long, then squeezes short.
quests.explanation: An earthworm moves by lengthening and shortening its body. Tiny bristles on its skin grip the soil.
quests.funFact: An earthworm has five pairs of tiny heart-like tubes.
quests.question: Worm

quests.instruction: Find the animal that digs a hole in warm sand with its back flippers and then buries its eggs in it.
quests.hint: It crawls out of the sea to do this job.
quests.explanation: A mother sea turtle scoops out a nest in the sand with her back flippers, lays her eggs and covers them.
quests.funFact: The temperature of the sand decides whether baby sea turtles will be boys or girls.
quests.question: Turtle

quests.instruction: Find the little animal that digs long burrows with separate rooms for sleeping and storing food.
quests.hint: Its front paws are strong little shovels.
quests.explanation: Wild hamsters dig deep burrows with different chambers for sleeping and for storing food.
quests.funFact: The word hamster comes from a German word meaning "to hoard".
quests.question: Hamster

quests.instruction: Pick the animal that glides along on a single muscular foot, over a trail of its own slime.
quests.hint: Ripples of muscle travel along its underside.
quests.explanation: A snail has one muscular foot. Waves of muscle push it forward over a layer of slime that helps it slide.
quests.funFact: A garden snail travels about 50 metres in an hour.
quests.question: Snail

quests.instruction: Which leaf-muncher crawls on six real legs at the front and stubby grippy legs further back?
quests.hint: The stubby extra legs hold onto leaves.
quests.explanation: A caterpillar has six true legs and several pairs of stubby, sticky prolegs that grip leaves as it crawls.
quests.funFact: A caterpillar can eat many times its own body weight in leaves in a single day.
quests.question: Caterpillar

quests.instruction: Name the animal that can walk upside down along a ceiling on eight legs.
quests.hint: Count how many legs it has.
quests.explanation: Spiders have eight legs, and tiny claws and hairs on their feet help them cling to walls and ceilings.
quests.funFact: A spider extends its legs by pumping fluid into them, a bit like tiny hydraulics.
quests.question: Spider

quests.instruction: Which animal escapes a chasing hunter by zigzagging across open ground on its powerful back legs?
quests.hint: Quick changes in direction confuse its chaser.
quests.explanation: A rabbit's strong hind legs give it bursts of speed, and zigzagging makes it hard for a hunter to catch.
quests.funFact: A wild rabbit can leap about a metre high when it is fleeing.
quests.question: Rabbit

quests.instruction: Which birds fly in a V shape, taking turns to lead, on long journeys?
quests.hint: Flying behind another bird means less work for them.
quests.explanation: In a V, each bird flies in the swirling air left behind by the bird ahead, which helps it use less energy. They swap places at the front.
quests.funFact: Wild ducks can fly for hours at around 60 kilometres an hour.
quests.question: Duck

quests.instruction: Pick the giant that looks slow and heavy but can charge at about 50 kilometres an hour.
quests.hint: Don't be fooled by its bulk.
quests.explanation: Rhinos are heavy, but they can charge fast in short bursts, which is why people shouldn't get near them.
quests.funFact: A big rhino can weigh more than a small car.
quests.question: Rhino

quests.instruction: Find the hunter that leaps high and dives headfirst into snow to catch a mouse it can only hear.
quests.hint: It listens first, then pounces from above.
quests.explanation: Foxes hear small animals moving beneath snow or grass, then jump up and pounce down on them.
quests.funFact: A fox's pupils are slits that run up and down, a bit like a cat's.
quests.question: Fox

quests.instruction: Which swimmer has to keep moving so that water keeps flowing over its gills?
quests.hint: If it stopped, it couldn't get enough oxygen.
quests.explanation: Some sharks must keep swimming so water flows over their gills. Others can rest on the seabed and pump water over them instead.
quests.funFact: Nurse sharks can lie still on the sea floor and pump water over their gills.
quests.question: Shark

quests.instruction: Name the hunter that creeps close, then explodes into a short sprint rather than chasing for long.
quests.hint: It gets close before it makes its move.
quests.explanation: Lions are sprinters. They sneak up as close as they can and rush, and if the prey gets away they usually give up.
quests.funFact: Lionesses do most of the hunting for their group.
quests.question: Lion

quests.instruction: Pick the bird that stands upright and waddles on land, but is graceful and fast in the water.
quests.hint: Its legs are set far back on its body.
quests.explanation: Penguins' legs sit far back on their bodies, so they stand upright and waddle. In water, their flipper-like wings make them fast swimmers.
quests.funFact: An emperor penguin can leap more than a metre out of the water onto the ice.
quests.question: Penguin

quests.instruction: Which long-legged bird often rests standing on one leg?
quests.hint: Tucking one leg up may help it save warmth.
quests.explanation: Standing on one leg may help a flamingo keep heat in, and it lets the other leg rest.
quests.funFact: Flamingos can even sleep while balancing on one leg.
quests.question: Flamingo

quests.instruction: Find the animal that leaps out of the water in arcs as it travels fast, saving energy.
quests.hint: In the air there is less drag than in water.
quests.explanation: At high speed, leaping through the air meets less resistance than pushing through the water, so dolphins often leap as they travel.
quests.funFact: A dolphin can leap several metres above the surface.
quests.question: Dolphin
